attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No actual endpoint-box values f_v(±h), f_v(±2h), f_v(±3h), no sharp M_{8,v}, and no certified E_tail have been computed for the Yang-Mills endpoint geometry.
steps: Contract the post-H,K endpoint boundary OPE with the Feshbach null vector alpha=(1,1,-2), so only the scalar null-channel polarization is needed.
Use the connected log Z_v(s) to identify the irreducible endpoint cumulant as kappa_v(alpha)=d^4/ds^4 log Z_v(s)|_{0}=<X_v^4>_c.
Check cancellations before estimating signs: the fourth connected derivative removes disconnected Wick-square pieces, and the null incidence identity kills the straight C_A f f boundary contact.
Solve the symmetric seven-point moment equations for a fourth derivative stencil: c0+2(c1+c2+c3)=0, c1+4c2+9c3=0, 2(c1+16c2+81c3)=24, and c1+64c2+729c3=0. This gives c0=28/3, c1=-13/2, c2=2, c3=-1/6.
The eighth-moment residue is 2(c1+256c2+6561c3)/8!=-7/240, hence |kappa_v-D_h f_v|<=7h^4 M_{8,v}/240.

Insert the color/geometric factor (g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2, endpoint orientation weights omega_v, and the tail interval to form I_end. The valid finite-block decision is now interval arithmetic on M_G+I_end.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is a valid reduction and error formula, but the sign of M_G+R_end is still unknown until the same-theory endpoint heat-kernel integrals or a scale-sharp analytic bound are supplied.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Endpoint kappa_4 scalar certification for the post-H,K Wilson block

assumptions: The regulator is the reflection-positive heat-kernel plaquette action on a fixed endpoint box B_v before the continuum limit.
The localized source keeps log Z_v(s) C^8 for |s|<=3h, with a certified bound M_{8,v} on |d^8/ds^8 log Z_v(s)|.
Endpoint boxes cover all corners where the reflected hairpin sheets meet the boundary; the complement is controlled by a tail bound E_tail.
Straight boundary-edge incidences satisfy the null identity for alpha, so the local C_A f f contact has zero null-channel contraction.
The connected log partition function is used, so disconnected Wick-square contributions are not counted inside kappa_v; their remaining Gram part is nonnegative and safe.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel regulated endpoint box Z_v(s) for the plaquette sheet, with localized singlet source s Xi_v obtained from the Feshbach null incidence alpha=(1,1,-2) and parallel-transported endpoint plaquette fluxes.
target object: the scalar post-H,K Schur-Feshbach endpoint correction S_null=M_G+R_end+Tail for the locked three-hairpin Wilson OS block.

controlled interface: replace the connected boundary-OPE polarization R in the null channel by same-regulator endpoint source derivatives of log Z_v, preserving the Wilson collar normalization already used for H and K.

same-theory condition: the source is only a derivative probe at s=0 of the original heat-kernel Wilson measure; no boundary counterterm, altered Wilson-loop renormalization, or enlarged observable algebra is introduced.
X_v=<Xi_v,F_v> is the singlet endpoint flux insertion; F_v denotes plaquette curvatures parallel transported to v.
M_G is the already certified positive Gaussian Schur-Feshbach margin after the H,K computation; it is not recomputed in this cycle.

equations.label: straight ff contact cancellation
equations.valid_when: Valid when the three hairpin footprints have the same oriented straight-edge incidence used in the H,K block.

equations.label: seven point fourth derivative stencil
equations.valid_when: Valid when log Z_v is evaluated at the seven same-theory source strengths 0, plus or minus h, 2h, and 3h.

equations.label: stencil remainder
equations.valid_when: Valid when the eighth source derivative of log Z_v is bounded throughout the interval |s|<=3h.

equations.label: certified endpoint interval
equations.valid_when: Valid when endpoint weights omega_v encode the actual null-channel orientation and all non-endpoint contributions are included in E_tail.

equations.label: promotion and falsifier sign test
equations.valid_when: Valid when M_G is the previously normalized Schur-Feshbach margin and the interval encloses every endpoint and tail error.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier occurs if the certified interval has sup(M_G+I_end)<0, or if the source derivative cannot be identified with the same-theory Wilson boundary OPE at s=0.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma turns the remaining R/kappa_4 handoff term into a finite, regulator-level scalar computation with explicit color factor, incidence weights, and certified error.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator, the post-H,K null-channel endpoint contribution is a same-theory scalar fourth source derivative of the endpoint-box log partition function. A seven-point central stencil gives a certified interval for this connected kappa_4 term with error 7 h^4 M_8/240; the valid promotion or falsifier test is the sign of the interval for M_G+R_end.

assumptions: The endpoint box contains finitely many plaquettes and links at fixed regulator a.
The source factor is bounded for |s|<=3h after the endpoint flux variables are represented by heat-kernel derivatives.
The heat-kernel character series is truncated symmetrically in representations and conjugates.
definitions: K_t(U) is the SU(N) heat kernel used in every plaquette of the endpoint box.
Lambda_L is a finite set of irreducible representations with C_2(lambda)<=L.
The source insertion is kept inside the endpoint box, so reflection positivity of the surrounding collar is not altered.

equations.label: heat kernel character expansion
equations.valid_when: Valid when the endpoint box uses the standard compact-group heat-kernel plaquette regulator at positive heat time t_a.

equations.label: L2 truncation tail
equations.valid_when: Valid when the cutoff Lambda_L is imposed on irreducible representations in the Peter-Weyl expansion.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the character tail or source-derivative constants blow up too fast as a decreases, this computation remains finite-regulator only and cannot promote the continuum bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Provides a concrete way to generate the seven values entering the scalar kappa_4 stencil.
candidate_lemmas.statement: At fixed lattice spacing and endpoint-box size, each value f_v(jh) is a compact SU(N) heat-kernel integral and can be computed with a character cutoff; the truncation tail gives a deterministic route to the seven source evaluations.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot only if the source derivative cannot be made same-theory or if endpoint/tail bounds are nonuniform enough to destroy every certified interval.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the finite hairpin block if the computed interval satisfies inf(M_G+I_end)>0 with cutoff-stable M_8 and tail bounds.
control_decision.reason: The branch made a valid contribution beyond the stored threshold by reducing the remaining R term to certified same-theory source evaluations with explicit error and sign criteria.

dependency_updates.description: Exact seven-source formula and 7h^4 M_8/240 error bound for the null-channel endpoint connected kappa_4.
Must identify the source derivative of log Z_v at s=0 with the original Wilson boundary OPE cumulant without adding boundary renormalization.
Need heat-kernel character or compact-group quadrature values for f_v at 0, ±h, ±2h, ±3h in the actual endpoint geometry.
Need cutoff-uniform or scale-sharp bounds for E_tail and M_8 to pass from finite regulator certification to the continuum bridge.

falsifiers: Certified upper endpoint interval sup(M_G+I_end)<0; this is the direct finite-block falsifier for same-theory OS positivity in the post-H,K null channel.
Failure of the straight-edge incidence identity after parallel transport conventions are fixed; then the C_A f f contact was wrongly canceled.
A nonzero boundary counterterm is needed to define Z_v(s) or its fourth derivative; this breaks the same-theory condition even if the modified matrix is positive.
The eighth-derivative or tail bounds diverge so strongly under cutoff removal that no valid continuum endpoint interval survives.
Endpoint character truncation reveals a large negative connected kappa_4 contribution exceeding the Gaussian margin for every admissible h.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 251 turns the scalar endpoint-kappa_4 plan into an exact certified stencil. The new contribution is the explicit seven-point fourth-derivative formula, its 7h^4 M_8/240 error, and the interval sign test for the post-H,K endpoint term. The regulator is the heat-kernel plaquette sheet; the cumulant is <X_v^4>_c from log Z_v; the cancellations are connected Wick-square removal and straight C_A f f null-incidence cancellation. The branch is not looping, but it now needs actual endpoint-box data or a sharp analytic M_8/tail estimate.
